title: Can AI systems have free will?
abstract: arXiv:2609.15407v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: While there has been much discussion of whether AI systems could function as moral agents or acquire sentience, there has been very little discussion of whether AI systems could have free will. I sketch a framework for thinking about this question, inspired by Daniel Dennett's work. I argue that, to determine whether an AI system has free will, we should not look for some mysterious property, expect its underlying algorithms to be indeterministic, or ask whether the system is unpredictable. Rather, we should simply ask whether we have good explanatory reasons to view the system as an intentional agent, with the capacity for choice between alternative possibilities and control over the resulting actions. If the answer is "yes", then the system counts as having free will in a pragmatic and diagnostically useful sense.

translated_title: 人工智能系统能拥有自由意志吗？
translated_abstract: 关于人工智能系统能否作为道德主体运作或获得感知能力，学界已有诸多讨论，但关于AI系统能否拥有自由意志的探讨却十分稀少。本文借鉴丹尼尔·丹尼特的研究成果，勾勒出一个思考这一问题的框架。我认为，要判断一个AI系统是否拥有自由意志，我们不应去寻找某种神秘的属性，不应期待其底层算法是非决定论的，也不应追问该系统是否不可预测。相反，我们应该简单地问：我们是否有充分的解释性理由将该系统视为一个具有意向性的主体，即拥有在多种可能性之间进行选择的能力，以及控制由此产生的行为的能力。如果答案是肯定的，那么该系统就可以被视为拥有自由意志——一种实用主义的、且具有诊断价值的自由意志概念。
tldr: 本文借鉴丹尼特的哲学思想提出，判断AI系统是否拥有自由意志无需寻找神秘属性或非决定论算法，只需基于解释性理由判断其能否被视为一个具有选择能力与行为控制能力的意向性主体。
en_tdlr: Inspired by Daniel Dennett's work, this paper argues that determining whether AI systems have free will requires no mysterious properties or indeterministic algorithms—we only need good explanatory reasons to view the system as an intentional agent capable of choice and control over its actions.
